meta.title: Direct Share — Encrypted P2P File Transfer over WebRTC
meta.description: Send files straight from your device to your peer's over WebRTC. The server only introduces peers; files never pass through it and are never stored.

hero.title:
Send the file directly,
no middleman.
hero.lead: Your files travel from your device to your friend's over an encrypted channel — the server only introduces you and never sees a single byte. No upload, no storage, no server limits.
hero.note: Encrypted by default (DTLS/SRTP) · No file is ever stored on any server

app.heading: Start sharing
app.sub: Create a room and share its link, or enter your friend's room code. The session ends automatically when both peers leave, and no file trace remains on any server.

how.heading: How it works
how.sub: Only three steps, and your files stay between the two devices from start to finish.
how.s1d: The signaling server (Node.js + Socket.io) only exchanges SDP offers and ICE candidates between the two devices. It never sees a byte of your files.
how.s2d: Both browsers open an RTCDataChannel encrypted with DTLS/SRTP and traverse NAT via STUN/TURN.
how.s3d: The file is split into 64KB chunks and sent in order with automatic backpressure when the channel fills, then reassembled and size-verified.

security.heading: Security first
security.sub: Four classic P2P vulnerabilities — and how we fixed them here:
security.s1d: A malicious payload or huge stream exhausts browser memory (DoS).
security.s1f: A maximum file size, strict metadata and per-chunk size validation, and a signaling payload cap on the server.
security.s2d: STUN reveals the peer's public or local IP.
security.s2f: TURN server support to hide the IP and relay through a secure middlebox — configured via environment variables.
security.s3d: Intercepting unencrypted Socket.io signals to swap encryption keys.
security.s3f: Deploy over WSS/HTTPS + built-in WebRTC encryption + an optional AES-256-GCM layer with a key the server never knows.
security.s4d: Guessing a short room code and joining to steal files.
security.s4f: Random UUID v4 codes, a scrypt-hashed password, join-attempt limiting, and the room is destroyed the moment the last device leaves.

features.heading: Professional features
features.sub: Everything you need to move large files safely and fast, with no intermediary service.
features.f1d: Pause, then resume from the last acknowledged chunk instead of starting over.
features.f2d: Every chunk encrypted with AES-GCM and a unique random IV, using a key derived from the room code and password — the server never knows it.
features.f3d: Drag & drop UI, a real progress bar, live transfer speed (MB/s) and a computed ETA.
features.f4d: The file is wiped from both sides' memory as soon as the download completes — total privacy (Burn on Read).
features.f5d: Send multiple files in sequence within the same session without reconnecting.
features.f6d: Peer-to-multipoint broadcast and mesh networking — recorded as a future extension.

dev.heading: About the developer
dev.sub: From idea to code: interface design, transfer protocol, and security hardening.
dev.name: Zerrouki Ahmed Mouadh
dev.bio: Built this project as a hands-on example of encrypted browser-to-browser file transfer with no middleman server: a light web UI, a chunking and resume protocol, and a tiny signaling server that never touches your data.
